title: Press archive
manifesto: Not a news ticker — an outside audit. Each entry is on-the-record journalism documenting facts in the Lagovsky case.

items.title: Awaiting extradition: the Justice Minister holds the last word
items.summary: Nearly six months without a signature from Nenad Vuić. Courts have done their part; what remains is an unappealable ministerial order. No work permit, no health insurance, a family of four in limbo.
items.focus: Counsel Vladimir Hrle told RFE Serbia must not surrender anyone to a real risk under Article 3 ECHR. The piece ties legal deadlock to human cost — children, mobilisation, a year of uncertainty.

items.title: Appeal court wouldn't touch the defence — only Moscow's bundle
items.summary: Judges said they cared about the received file, not whether the charge stacks up. Russian arbitration? Not on the table.
items.focus: Štambuk flagged missing reasonable suspicion and Russia's exit from anti-torture treaties. N1 — CNN's Balkan partner — put that on the public record.

items.title: Belgrade family caught between deportation and the draft
items.summary: Nova ran the human story: teenagers in Serbian schools, a nurse supporting four people, extradition papers at the minister's desk.
items.focus: Asylum filing underscores Serbia's duty to test the threat before any surrender.

items.title: Serbia one ministerial signature away from extradition
items.summary: 3 December: appeal court says grounds are met. After that, only politics.
items.focus: Štambuk's blunt take: ministers rarely say no once judges say yes. RFE put the case on Europe's radar.

press_call.title: For journalists
press_call.text: Arbitration, extradition, asylum, Interpol — primary documents and defence filings are open. Ask for anything.
press_call.thesis: Serbia isn't extraditing a fugitive. It's extraditing a lawyer who drafted a lawful contract. If that stands, international law is just paperwork.
